Cc: CloudOps Solutions <eng-sales@cloudops.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: QBR infra: capacity & GPU unit economics — planning notes

Team — kicking this off so we have a crisp deliverable for Leadership QBR next week. Goal: present a single-slide recommendation and appendix with the numbers that justify it. High-level asks below; details/attachments included.

One-paragraph summary to prepare for the slide: where we sit on GPU economics today, where we expect to be at the end of Q2 given product roadmaps and bookings, and the recommended capacity posture (reserve / burst / fallbacks) with cost delta.

Current context (short):
- Avg production GPU utilization: ~62% over last 30d, heavy variance on demo days and large-model training runs (p95 nights up to ~89%).
- Token cost pressure from two angles: model growth (longer sequences) and more tail requests with low batching opportunity.
- We have options that tranche cost reduction vs latency risk: batching policies, more aggressive quantization, increased KV caching, and reserved vs on-demand mixes.

Immediate asks (owners & deadlines):
1) Marcus — attach a 1-page cost table: current monthly GPU spend, forecast (baseline/conservative/aggressive), and per-token unit cost under proposed batching/quantization settings. Due EOD Wed (04/07).
2) Vivek — ops constraints: what batching levels are safe for p50/p90/p95; what fallback / canary routing we need to keep latency SLOs when batching spikes. Due Thu morning (04/08).
3) Laura — customer/sales implications: how much buffer we should hold for demos/enterprise events and whether we can gate pricing changes. Note any renewals next quarter that need capacity guarantees. Due Thu EOD.
4) Evelyn — will validate the three-scenario framing (conservative/baseline/aggressive) and confirm whether leadership wants cost-pass-through options on pricing.

Attachments: gpu_costs_q2.xlsx (raw numbers), batching-summary.pdf (initial tradeoffs).

Please keep replies inline and preserve the numbers — we will stitch into the QBR deck on Friday.

Thanks,
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra

Subject: Re: QBR infra: capacity & GPU unit economics — planning notes

Rishi — attached the spreadsheet slice and a short summary. High-level bullets from the numbers:
- Baseline (status quo): ~$1.28M/month GPU spend, avg util 62%, effective token cost $0.0039/token (in-hosting mix + reserved amortization).
- Conservative (more reserved capacity to avoid throttles): +14% cost, reduces p95 queueing but increases idle during off-peak.
- Aggressive (optimize for unit cost): -18% cost vs baseline if we move 60% of flows to 8-bit quantized instances and increase batching. Latency increases at p95 by ~40ms on average in our microbenchmarks.

Batching/caching specifics in spreadsheet:
- Naive batching (no priority): throughput +22%, best-effort latency at p50 maintained; p95 affected depending on workload mix.
- Batching with routing by SLA: throughput +16% with p95 preservation for enterprise customers.
- KV prefix caching: for steady-state queries (search-like patterns) we see 12-20% token-cost reduction; for chat flows with long contexts caching has diminishing returns.

Notes / assumptions: GPU price per hour uses committed pricing blended with on-demand bursts (we assume 40% reserved pool, 60% burstable). Quantization savings assume minimal model quality regression for current prompt sets; need eval confirmation.

Attachment: gpu_costs_q2.xlsx (tabs: baseline, scenarios, batching_models)

—Marcus
Senior Dir, Capacity Planning
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>, evelyn_hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: QBR infra: capacity & GPU unit economics — planning notes

Thanks Marcus — a couple of ops clarifications to make the scenarios actionable:

1) Safe batching envelope: we can safely batch up to 40 reqs/window for low-priority/background routes without needing additional capacity; for mixed-priority production traffic we should target ~20 reqs/window and maintain dynamic bypass when queueing >200ms.
2) Canary plan for quantization: prefer a gradual rollout by route (non-critical internal tooling -> public API) with continuous eval against our quality prompts. If we run into repeat degradations, auto-fallback to FP16 varients is required.
3) Autoscale and reserved mix: ops recommendation is 50% reserved, 30% committed burst pool, 20% on-demand. This preserves steady cost predictability while allowing capacity elastic bursts on major demo/launch days.

Operational risks: heavy batching can amplify tail latency under adversarial request patterns; we should instrument early and add a short-circuit path for time-sensitive tokens. Also, ensure tracing + per-route token counting is enabled in the next 72 hours for accurate billing attribution.

I’ll add a one-page ops appendix that defines fail-open rules and instrumentation checks. Due Thu morning.

—Vivek
Head of Infrastructure Reliability
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 13:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: QBR infra: capacity & GPU unit economics — planning notes

Rishi — thanks for the outline. A couple of items from GTM/Customer success perspective:
- Buffer sizing: Sales asks a clear minimum guaranteed capacity for top-10 enterprise accounts. For QBR slide, please include the delta cost to guarantee an additional 20% headroom for those accounts (feel free to use Marcus’s conservative scenario numbers).
- Demo days: historically (last 6 months) we see up to 3x baseline request rate on major marketing demos; recommend a temporary burst policy that locks in capacity 72 hours prior and auto-scales down after 24 hours.
- Pricing: we should surface a pricing appendix that shows the cost-pass-through options (no pass-through, partial surcharge, full surcharge) with simple examples for a 1M token/month customer.

I’ll pull the renewal list and annotate which accounts expect SLAs. Will drop a note by Thu EOD.

—Laura
VP, Revenue Operations

To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: QBR infra: capacity & GPU unit economics — planning notes

Thank you — good, pragmatic framing. Leadership asks:
1) Three scenarios (conservative / baseline / aggressive) with clear cost delta and one-sentence business impact.
2) For each scenario: expected p50/p90/p95 latency impact and key mitigations.
3) A proposed recommendation (single preferred scenario) and an optional contingency (what we do if bookings exceed forecast by >20%).

EOD Friday for the consolidated QBR packet. Rishi, please ensure the slide includes an appendix link to Marcus’s spreadsheet + Vivek’s ops appendix. Also highlight any decisions that require exec sign-off (reserved capacity commitments > $Xk/month).

—Evelyn
SVP, Product & Ops

- Ops appendix: Vivek (Thu morning).
- GTM appendix & renewal flags: Laura (Thu EOD).
- Attachments to include: gpu_costs_q2.xlsx, batching-summary.pdf, qbr_infra_playbook_notes.txt

Decision points for execs:
- Whether to move to 50% reserved (ops recommended) or keep 40% reserved to save immediate cash.
- Whether to approve a controlled quantization rollout across non-enterprise routes.

If no material objections, I’ll compile the deck Friday and circulate for 1-hour dry run on Monday AM before the QBR.
